messages:
maria: seeing repeated gRPC streaming stalls between pods in different AZs on the new overlay. High-level: long pauses ~2-5s then resume. Affected: model-serving and some GPU training sidecars.
ashwin: ack, can you paste a tcpdump + ip link? suspecting fragmentation due to encapsulation overhead.
maria: tcpdump shows lots of retransmits on the TCP stream and a `<DF>` flagged packet followed by fragmented reassembly on the node logs. quick snippet: `IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 12345, offset 0, flags [DF])` then kernel logs: `ip_frag:  dropped` a few times.
jen: are we using VXLAN with GSO/GRO enabled? overlay adds 50-70 bytes. If pod MTU still 1500, outer headers push it over path MTU.
maria: overlay is VXLAN, host MTU is 9001 on some nodes (jumbo), but the ENI/physical path through transit gateways has 1500 in some hops. weirdly only certain node pairs affected.
sam: gpu-fleet chiming in: training jobs show stall patterns aligned with big tensor checkpoint transfers (~>1MB writes over gRPC) — smaller calls fine.
ashwin: that matches fragmentation causing gRPC send/recv stalls when reassembly slows down. two quick mitigations while we debug: 1) reduce pod MTU to 1400; 2) force GSO/GRO on host for encaps interfaces.
jen: commands to check: `ip link show dev <iface>` and `ethtool -k <iface>` to see `gso`/`gro`/`tso`. to test MTU path use `ping -M do -s <size> <peer>` to identify the PMTU.
maria: ran `ping -M do -s 1372 <peer>` worked, `1373` failed. outer encap overhead ~50 so logical pod MTU ~1422.
infra-bot: noticed route flaps between node-17 and node-42 at 2026-03-12T09:34:10Z, switching through different transit instances.
ashwin: inter-AZ transit change could hit a non-jumbo hop. that explains node-pair variance. we should mark nodes with non-jumbo path in our inventory.
sam: workaround test result: lowering pod MTU to 1400 for a service prevented stalls for 24h. cost: minor perf hit but stable.
jen: other option: enable `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on nodes to help kernel discover MTU and avoid blackholing. also check `sysctl net.ipv4.ipfrag_high_thresh` if fragmentation queue is saturating.
maria: tried `tcp_mtu_probing=1` on one node, saw fewer stalls but reassembly drops still show up occasionally.
ashwin: long term we should: (a) reconcile MTU across transit/peering, (b) configure overlay to use GSO-friendly encaps (or increase inner segment sizes), (c) add a deployment-level MTU annotation and default to 1400 for cross-AZ traffic.
sam: +1 - for GPU jobs we can add a job template that sets MTU and pins to nodes with jumbo support.
jen: also open question: does RDMA offload bypass reassembly issues? not currently used for these services. RDMA would avoid TCP stack, but not feasible for model-serving.
maria: i'll roll a canary lowering MTU on the affected service and watch. leaving logs & tcpdump collection enabled. thanks. :thumbsup:
ashwin: if you get a repro, drop pcap and I'll run `tracepath` + `tc` qdisc inspect. we should add a playbook for MTU/encap debugging.
maria: noted. pushing changes now. will update thread when canary stabilizes. :rocket:
